terms.comment: Tibullus’s words for the dry weeks of high summer under the Dog Star. Latin otherwise names the season by the summer, aestās, the dry season of the Mediterranean, or by its dryness, siccitās (see “drought”).

terms.gloss: dryness of the weather, a dry spell; in the plural, dry seasons

phrases.latin: cum ex longā siccitāte aestātis terra caret ūmōre pluviātilī
phrases.english: when after the long dryness of summer the earth lacks rainwater

phrases.latin: quod eō annō frūmentum in Galliā propter siccitātēs angustius prōvēnerat
phrases.english: because that year the corn had come up more sparsely in Gaul for the dry weather

phrases.latin: Aestāte hīc numquam ferē pluit; herba ārēscit.
phrases.english: In the dry season it hardly ever rains here; the grass dries up.

sources: Lewis & Short: siccus · Lewis & Short: aestas · Lewis & Short: siccitas
